correctness.rationale: Independent replay: python /workspace/branches/audit5.py. The program generates the 1440 column-ordered six-rook words and 3600 deleted-column equations from the capacities, and the 15-by-20 inclusion equations from subsets. The orientation sign (-1)^j is constant within each boundary row and does not change its kernel; the separate column-action sign is retained. The ranks modulo 101 are 1435 and 15, giving rational lower bounds. Lifting the free-coordinate vectors to integers, checking every original integer boundary equation, and using their identity projections proves both upper bounds and integral saturation. This gives a different pair of integral bases. All three row generators act trivially and the column action on the entire basis is verified. Using only a generating 6-cycle and transposition gives a 50-equation intertwiner system of rank 24 over Q. Its primitive integer generator has determinant -162 and Smith factors (1,3,3,3,6), reproducing the reported quotient in the independent bases. Primitivity on a rational line forces every integral map to be an integer multiple, hence index 162|k|^5. There are no higher simplices, so the top kernel is H5 integrally. Young's rule for the subset modules and surjectivity of W over Q leave precisely S^(3,3) in L, and the nonzero determinant transfers the representation to K. The frozen proof/checker and captured matrix evidence were inspected, not executed.
